prompt.context_jp: 営業部から史上最年少の受賞者___出たとあって、山崎柊一の周りには すでに祝いの声が集まっていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 営業部から史上最年少の受賞者___出た
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits — the youngest-ever winner appearing is new, newsworthy information.

feedback.correct_en: が introduces the youngest-ever winner as newly reported information — this is why everyone is gathering around him. は would presuppose him as an already-established topic.
feedback.incorrect_en: は treats the winner as given/old information, which doesn't fit a 'news breaking out' context. を would make 受賞者 a direct object, but 出た here is intransitive.

contrast_examples.jp: その事故は大きかった。
contrast_examples.en: That accident was big. (already known topic)

prompt.context_jp: 経理の島は静か。営業部だけが騒いでいる場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 営業部の華やかな笑い声だけ___、静かなフロアに響き渡っていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle: 'only the sales dept's laughter' as the one and only thing echoing.

feedback.correct_en: 〜だけが marks exhaustive identification — among all the sounds, that laughter alone is what echoes. は would weaken the 'nothing else, only this' feel.
feedback.incorrect_en: だけは would shift to contrast ('as for only that, …'), losing the exhaustive 'that and nothing else is what rings out' nuance. に doesn't fit the subject slot.

contrast_examples.en: He alone doesn't know (contrast with others).

prompt.context_jp: ボスが経理部という職場について一般論を語る場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: そういうもんだよ 経理部___ 数字が合って当たり前
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle: the boss sets 'the accounting department' as the topic he's generalizing about.

feedback.correct_en: は frames 経理部 as the topic for a general statement — 'as for accounting, matching numbers is the baseline.' が would sound like identifying who matches numbers.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce 経理部 as new/identifying info, which clashes with the explanatory tone. で would mean 'at the accounting dept' as a location, missing the topic framing.

prompt.context_jp: 職人の勘が優れている人物として一人を特定する場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: その勘が優れているの___ 留田さんなんです
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle that identifies Tomeda as THE one with the superior intuition.

feedback.correct_en: 〜のが X です is the exhaustive-listing structure — 'the one whose intuition is excellent is (none other than) Tomeda.' は would sound like comparing/contrasting him with others.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would introduce contrast or old-topic framing, which doesn't fit a reveal/identification. を doesn't fit the copular pattern.

contrast_examples.en: The one who is the criminal is him. (exhaustive identification)

prompt.context_jp: 驚きのニュースを伝える場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 留田辰彦___来ます
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle: breaking news — Tomeda is coming!

feedback.correct_en: が presents the legendary Tomeda as brand-new, shocking information — the whole room erupts because this subject is fresh news. は would make it feel like he's already the known topic.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would be flat ('as for Tomeda, he's coming'), losing the dramatic reveal. も would mean 'Tomeda too,' implying others are also coming.

contrast_examples.en: The president is coming tomorrow. (known topic)

prompt.context_jp: 沙名子が有休について原則を述べる場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 有休___ 社員の正当な権利ですから
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle: she states a principle about annual leave as the topic.

feedback.correct_en: は sets 有休 as the topic for a general principle — 'as for paid leave, it's a legitimate right.' This is a definitional statement, not news.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would identify paid leave as THE right (odd here). を would make it an object, but the predicate is a nominal 'is a right.'

prompt.context_jp: 藤見を社員に推薦したのが誰かを明かす場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 留田さんなんです 藤見さんを社員に推薦したの___
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle: revealing WHO recommended her — Tomeda, no one else.

feedback.correct_en: In this cleft structure (A is B), 'the one who recommended her' is the topic/known info, so は fits. The surprise/new info is 留田さん on the other side.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make the recommender itself new/unknown, but it's the already-raised question. を doesn't fit the copular slot.

prompt.context_jp: 留田さんの担当業務を説明する場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 留田さん___窯焚き製法の担当だから
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle: 'As for Mr. Tomeda, he's in charge of…'

feedback.correct_en: は sets Tomeda as the topic to be described. The listener already knows who he is; this sentence adds info about him.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would suddenly spotlight him as new news. も would mean 'Tomeda too (is in charge),' implying others.

contrast_examples.en: He is a doctor. (describing a known person)

prompt.context_jp: 沙名子の歩幅が自然と山田のそれと一致していく場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼女の歩幅は自然と山田のそれ___合っていた
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle: her stride matched his.

feedback.correct_en: 合う takes に to mark what something matches with — her stride aligned to his. で (means) and を (object) don't work here.
feedback.incorrect_en: で would mark a location or means, not a target of matching. を would make 'his' a direct object, which 合う doesn't take.

prompt.context_jp: 沙名子が思わず息を呑む場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 沙名子は思わず息___呑んだ
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle: 'gasped' uses 息 as the object of 呑む.

feedback.correct_en: 息を呑む is a fixed expression ('to gasp / catch one's breath') — 息 is the direct object of 呑む.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make 息 a subject, which breaks the idiom. に would mark a target, which doesn't fit.

contrast_examples.en: To get out of breath. (息 is the subject here — different idiom)

prompt.context_jp: 沙名子が静かに仕事に集中しようとしている場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 沙名子は...いつも通り伝票の点検___集中しようとしていた
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle: 'to focus on invoice checking.'

feedback.correct_en: 集中する takes に to mark what you concentrate on. を would be ungrammatical with this verb.
feedback.incorrect_en: を doesn't pair with 集中する. で would mark a means/location, not the target of focus.

prompt.context_jp: 吉村を揶揄する発言。「あのザル村___ 自分が受賞したわけでもないのに」
prompt.prompt_jp: あのザル村___ 自分が受賞したわけでもないのに
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that singles out 'that Zaru-mura' contrastively.

feedback.correct_en: は picks out 'that Zaru-mura' and contrasts him with how he SHOULD be acting (not his own win). It's a topicalized complaint about him specifically.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce him as new info, but he's already the known target of the complaint. も would mean 'Zaru-mura also,' which doesn't fit.

contrast_examples.jp: あいつは何考えてるんだ。
contrast_examples.en: That guy — what's he thinking?! (singled-out complaint)

prompt.context_jp: 山崎の若さに驚く発言。
prompt.prompt_jp: 山崎さん___受賞するのって いつも おじさんばっかなのに
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle: Yamazaki is the admired topic being commented on.

feedback.correct_en: は raises Yamazaki as the known topic ('Mr. Yamazaki — he's amazing'). The surprise is about him in contrast to the usual old-guy winners.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make him newly presented, but he's clearly the current subject of conversation. に doesn't fit a human subject in this frame.

contrast_examples.en: Mr. Tanaka is amazing. (comment on known person)
It's Mr. Tanaka who is amazing. (identifying)

prompt.context_jp: 佐々木が出張申請書の中に、憧れの職人の名前を見つける場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 見慣れた仙台工場の名の下に、彼女が長年密かに憧れてきた名前___刻まれていた
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle: a new name is being discovered on the page.

feedback.correct_en: が presents the admired name as new, startling information that Sasaki notices on the page — this triggers her reaction.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would frame the name as already-known topic, missing the moment-of-discovery feel. を doesn't fit an intransitive 刻まれる.

contrast_examples.en: That letter is on the desk. (known topic)

prompt.context_jp: 沙名子を評する地の文。
prompt.prompt_jp: 経理の綱領を誰よりも厳しく守る沙名子___その真剣な声には耳を傾けざるを得ない
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for 'even Sanako, who…, cannot help but listen.'

feedback.correct_en: でさえ ('even') marks Sanako as the extreme case — even she, the strictest, has to listen. が/を don't combine with さえ this way as a subject marker.
feedback.incorrect_en: がさえ is ungrammatical in modern Japanese for this slot. をさえ would need a transitive object.

contrast_examples.jp: 子供でさえ知っている。

prompt.context_jp: 後ろから声をかけられ、山田が反応する場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 呼ばれた山田の背中___ ほんの一瞬こわばる
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle: a sudden, noticed micro-reaction in his back.

feedback.correct_en: が spotlights the observed physical event — his back stiffening is noticed in the moment. は would background it as a general property.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make it feel like a known/habitual topic rather than a flash observation. を doesn't fit the intransitive こわばる.

contrast_examples.en: His face was (as for the face) red. (describing)

prompt.context_jp: 沙名子が領収書を丁重に突き返す場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 申し訳ございませんが このままでは 経費で___ことができません
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the verb: 'these can't be ___ as expenses.'

feedback.correct_en: 経費で落とす is the set collocation meaning 'to write off as a business expense.' This idiom is the very title motif of the show.
feedback.incorrect_en: 下げる means 'to lower'; 降りる is intransitive 'to get off/descend.' Neither pairs with 経費 in this sense.

contrast_examples.jp: これは経費で落とせません。
タクシー代を経費で落とす。
contrast_examples.en: To write off the taxi fare as an expense.

prompt.context_jp: 吉村が部下の受賞を自分の手柄のように誇る場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 上司の吉村は自分のことのように___を高くし
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the body part: idiom meaning 'to be proud/puffed up.'

feedback.correct_en: 鼻を高くする ('to lift one's nose') is a fixed idiom for being proud/boastful. It fits Yoshimura's puffed-up behavior perfectly.
feedback.incorrect_en: 肩を高くする isn't a set idiom (though 肩で風を切る exists). 目を高くする isn't idiomatic either.

contrast_examples.jp: 息子の受賞で鼻が高い。
contrast_examples.en: I'm proud of my son's award.

prompt.context_jp: 伝説の職人を迎える準備を部下に念押しする場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: かなり頑固な ___の方だと聞いている
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the compound: 'a stubborn, old-school craftsman type.'

feedback.correct_en: 職人かたぎ (職人気質) means 'craftsman temperament' — the stubborn, perfectionist disposition. It fits '頑固な○○の方.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 職人さん is just 'craftsman' and doesn't collocate with 頑固な…の方 here. 職人技 means 'craftsman's skill,' not a disposition.

contrast_examples.en: A father with a craftsman's temperament.

prompt.context_jp: 長年欠席していた留田が、急に授賞式へ来ると聞いた新発田の反応。
prompt.prompt_jp: どういう___の吹き回しだ
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the noun in this set phrase meaning 'what's gotten into…?'

feedback.correct_en: どういう風の吹き回し is a fixed idiom literally 'what way is the wind blowing?' — used to express surprise at a sudden change of behavior.
feedback.incorrect_en: 気 or 心 don't form this idiom. どういう気の迷い means something different ('what delusion is this?').

contrast_examples.jp: どういう風の吹き回しか、彼が謝ってきた。
contrast_examples.en: For some reason (lit. by which wind blowing), he apologized.

contrast_examples.jp: どういう風の吹き回し？

prompt.context_jp: デートに付き合うことに ようやく慣れてきた沙名子の心情。
prompt.prompt_jp: 仕事帰りのデートに付き合うのは、ようやく___ついてきたところだ
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the noun: idiom meaning 'to get the hang of / settle into.'

feedback.correct_en: 板につく means 'to become second nature / grow into a role.' It fits Sanako finally getting used to dating.
feedback.incorrect_en: 身につく means 'to acquire (a skill/habit)' — related but different grammar (身につける). 手につく doesn't form this idiom (手につかない does).

contrast_examples.jp: 司会業が板についてきた。
contrast_examples.en: He's really grown into the MC role.

prompt.context_jp: 工場長が自分からやって来たのを見ての部長のつぶやき。
prompt.prompt_jp: 飛んで火に入る夏の___
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the noun for this proverb: 'like a ___ flying into the fire.'

feedback.correct_en: 飛んで火に入る夏の虫 is a fixed proverb — 'a summer bug flying into the flame,' i.e. walking into one's own doom.
feedback.incorrect_en: 鳥 or 魚 are not the subject of this proverb. The image is specifically of moths/insects drawn to light.

contrast_examples.jp: まさに飛んで火に入る夏の虫だ。
contrast_examples.en: It's exactly like a moth to a flame.

prompt.context_jp: 工場長が、藤見さんを異動させようとした時の留田の様子を伝える。
prompt.prompt_jp: 俺も辞めてやるって ものすごい___で
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the noun: 'with an incredible ___' describing furious intensity.

feedback.correct_en: 剣幕 specifically means a furious, menacing demeanor. ものすごい剣幕で ('with great fury') is a standard collocation for angry outbursts.
feedback.incorrect_en: 迫力 means 'force/intensity' generally but doesn't carry the anger nuance. 元気 ('energy/health') is clearly wrong here.

contrast_examples.jp: ものすごい剣幕で怒鳴られた。
contrast_examples.en: I got yelled at with incredible fury.

prompt.context_jp: 沙名子が、見知らぬ訪問者に身元を尋ねる場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 失礼ですが ___で？
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the polite expression: 'Excuse me, but who are you?'

feedback.correct_en: どちら様 is the polite way to ask 'who are you?' in a business context. Sanako uses it to a stranger.
feedback.incorrect_en: だれ様 is not standard. なに様 means 'who do you think you are?!' — rude/confrontational.

contrast_examples.en: May I ask who you are?
Who do you think you are?! (hostile)

prompt.context_jp: ボスが経理部の仕事を自嘲気味に説明する。
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds more natural as the boss's generalization about accounting?

choices.text: 経理部は 数字が合って当たり前
経理部が 数字は合って当たり前

feedback.correct_en: A topicalizes 経理部 ('as for accounting') and lets 数字が state what matches. This is the natural topic-comment flow for a general truth about the department.
feedback.incorrect_en: B flips the markers: 経理部が newly identifies accounting (odd mid-explanation) and 数字は becomes contrastive, muddling the generalization.

prompt.context_jp: 上司のセクハラ発言に、沙名子がきっぱり拒絶する場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds more natural in Sanako's cool, formal register?

feedback.correct_en: 同意しかねます uses the formal 〜かねる pattern — polite but firm refusal. It matches Sanako's icy, by-the-book register.
feedback.incorrect_en: 同意できないです is grammatically fine but sounds softer/more casual, lacking the crisp professional bite Sanako delivers.

contrast_examples.en: I'm afraid I can't answer. (formal refusal)

prompt.context_jp: 沙名子が おずおずと、目の前の男性が留田本人かを確認する場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds more natural for Sanako's cautious, polite confirmation?

choices.text: もしかして あなたは… 留田辰彦さんで いらっしゃいますか？
もしかして あなたは… 留田辰彦さんで ありますか？

feedback.correct_en: 〜でいらっしゃいますか is the respectful (sonkeigo) form for asking 'are you Mr. X?' — exactly right for a careful first encounter.
feedback.incorrect_en: 〜でありますか is archaic/military-sounding and would feel bizarre in polite modern office speech.

contrast_examples.jp: 山田様でいらっしゃいますか？

prompt.context_jp: 佐々木が留田に失望している場面を美華がたしなめる。
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds more natural for 'it's not fair to be disappointed in him'?

choices.text: 相手に失望するのは フェアじゃないですよ
相手を失望するのは フェアじゃないですよ

feedback.correct_en: 失望する takes に to mark the target of the disappointment — '〜に失望する' is the fixed pattern.
feedback.incorrect_en: 〜を失望する is ungrammatical; 失望する is intransitive. (Compare transitive 失望させる 'to disappoint someone.')

prompt.context_jp: 山田がメールしてもいいかと聞いた直後、沙名子が条件をつける。
prompt.prompt_en: Which line matches Sanako's dry, boundary-setting style?

choices.text: 就業時間中はダメですよ
就業時間中にはダメですよ

feedback.correct_en: 就業時間中は uses は to contrast this time with others ('during work hours — no'). The implicit flip side is 'outside work hours is okay.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 就業時間中には sounds awkward; に+は together here loses the clean contrast and reads as redundant.

contrast_examples.en: On days off I don't work. (contrast with workdays)
